entry.title: Rise in accidents involving kids and e-bikes sparks debate about regulation
entry.summary: Emergency room departments are reporting soaring numbers of pediatric trauma accidents associated with micromobility devices. Experts and advocates agree that the federal government needs to step in.

entry.title: Sauna research gathers steam
entry.summary: Leading researchers in heat exposure are coming together to reach a consensus on what we know — and don't — about the health benefits of sauna and its potential for treating and preventing disease.

entry.title: Here's what to know if you're unsure about your measles immunity status
entry.summary: Vaccination is the best way to protect yourself against measles. For most adults, one shot of the MMR is considered enough protection. But there are certain situations that call for a second dose.

entry.title: How one antibiotic morning-after pill came to be widely available in San Francisco
entry.summary: An antibiotic morning-after pill has been shown to be effective for preventing STIs among gay men, but some doctors worry about antibiotic resistance. This story discusses STIs and their symptoms.

entry.title: Don't be scared: Being afraid is outright fun, and maybe useful
entry.summary: Listeners of NPR's Weekend Edition Sunday may already know that host Ayesha Rascoe loves horror. But why do scream queens (and kings) like her like what's frightening? The answer may surprise you.

entry.title: She was a global star: Teen bikes 700 miles carrying injured dad. Where is she now?
entry.summary: Her epic ride — carrying her injured dad on her $20 hot pink bicycle — made headlines. Promises were made — financial help, training for a cycling career, even a movie deal. Were any of them kept?

entry.title: Sweating the details: Sauna's potential health benefits draw scientists' interest
entry.summary: A group of international researchers is pushing to rigorously study the potential health benefits of sauna and other heat therapies. They hope to bring scientific legitimacy to the age-old practices.

entry.title: Ongoing lawsuits allege GLP-1s can cause serious harm. But we don't know how often
entry.summary: Scant data about serious adverse effects makes it harder to answer scientific and legal questions about how often the drugs might cause serious harm like blindness or pancreatitis.

entry.title: Did Russia play by the rules in reporting lab worker's death?
entry.summary: A global treaty signed by 197 countries — including Russia — requires reporting any death that could be a sign of an outbreak to come.

entry.title: ChatGPT for Teens has special safeguards. A watchdog group finds most don't work
entry.summary: A study from Common Sense Media says most safeguards in ChatGPT for Teens failed. The chatbot talks to teens like a friend and doesn't alert parents when users talk about self-harm and suicide.
